review:
This game has potential. This is still Early Access. It has flaws and bugs and the population has dwindled to really low levels. Overall the game is fun and I've had fun playing it. 

This review is intended for the Devs: When the game first launched, there were tens of thousands of players and the server lag was unbearable. We now have under 1000 players on any given cluster, but the underlying server issues haven't even been addressed by your team. This game will still not support anywhere near the amount of people you're falsely advertising as being able to support. If you want to salvage this game, you need to stop devoting resources to 'fluff' items, new creatures, new zones, and instead fully concentrate on fixing the problems underneath the hood first. Any large amount of people, like anything over 50, breaks the server. The server cannot handle the necessary transactions to allow smooth gameplay for the people in that particular tile. Throw on top of that any moving objects, like ships, tames, and anything else that's attached and you end up with a severely broken experience. Go to any island, populated or not, that has been built up either defensively or for pure roleplay and you end up with a broken experience. Some of these are the same problems experienced in ARK. This leads me to believe that there's probably a design flaw with this particular engine type and this way of using these game engines. You need to find a way to get around this particular limitation or you will never, ever, have a game that thousands of people can experience at once, let alone just a hundred of them in a tile. I, for one, can no longer handle the stuttering, frame sludge, rubber-banding, and general crappy performance. And the fact that you won't work on fixing it and would rather devote your resources to making 'new things', tells me that you have zero priority in actually making this game work properly. Show me I'm wrong.

This is one of the most painful reviews I've written, so let me tell you a story.

I loved this game. It was a childhood game dream come true. We were all hopeful for what was to be the decisive ocean-fairing open world survival game and for a time it was. I spent days of my time just sailing from point a to point b loving every second. I enjoyed the harsh circumstances that forced tactical, patient, and intelligent decisions that would literally decide what would happen for the next few hours. You can choose a faster and smaller ship and only take two hours to build, or opt for a larger ship that'll carry more but will be slower and take 8-12 hours to farm the materials.

I played with two friends who like me dedicated night and day to progressing our little band of merry men. We built a raft and sat on it for hours until we finally got to another island, and boy it was a once in a lifetime memory. We built our first single mast sloop. We farmed and farmed and farmed. We made a base, got animal tames, cosmetics, and just loved the everloving hell out the game and what it had to offer. We finally progressed to the point where we built a frigate. This thing took days to farm materials and was the end-all-be-all for naval combat, travel, and quite literally everything. If you weren't at an island, your home was your vessel. We built the frigate and named it something that filled all of us with pride. We went to sleep anticipating another day of amazing gameplay. Then, the Chinese came. 

You see the problem with Atlas was not the game itself, but it was the players. We logged in to discover our frigate, which we spent days farming for, was gone. We also noticed other ships that we became familiar with seeing shared the same fate. The Chinese, because they're Chinese (no literally), decided to sink any non-Chinese ship. We were just one of countless victims. So much so, in fact, that there are probably historical documentaries about the Europe-America war against the Chinese players -- it got that bad. 

Then, in similar fashion, Atlas suffered a content dry up and ultimately started to change things. In less than a few months the game had more or less died from mediocre and ignorant decisions that effectively made the only reasonable way of playing the game to join MASSIVE clans that treated you as literal slaves to do their bidding in the hopes that you may do something other than collect resources (think rust). Players like me tried to flee to private servers to play the game on our terms, until we found out each grid in the game is ran by its own server. So, if you wanted to play with the full map (with all content mind you) you were looking at somewhere between 100-200 dollars a month just to run the servers. 

We saw what was coming far before reality came, but we were ever hopeful. That is until they de facto dropped development of Atlas to focus on Ark. Ark is better for it, but Atlas is now just a wasteland with no place for refugees like me to go. I last played Atlas almost two years ago but I still think about how good of a game it was and how good it could've been had the right decisions been made. After finishing games like Dying Light, Elden Ring, and Dark Souls, it makes me pine for Atlas. 

I think back to how defining of an experience Atlas was for me, and as much as I want to play it, I hold to principle and just wish for better days.

Here's all I wanted, and should have reasonably expected from this pirate game:
I wanted to be able to build and maintain a small-ish boat that I could use to sail around, explore new islands, dig for treasure.  Maybe set up a small base on an island somewhere to store my loot.  And actually, all of that is possible!
I actually really, REALLY enjoyed the sailing.  The ocean looks incredible, and it's just really cool to build a boat, place the sails where you want them, paint the sails and the boat to your liking, climb up into the crow's nest and use your spyglass to scout out undiscovered lands, use the diving platform to go diving the very depths (although pretty much impossible since things kill you down there), and to sail up to islands, meet the residents who holed up there, and just explore.

The catch is, the boats take ridiculously long to grind up the materials to build for one person or a small group of people and are EASILY destroyed.  Ships of the Damned are annoying as hell, pop up into existence out of nowhere because the draw distance is so bad, and are just a pain to avoid.  Then if the SotD don't kill you, real human players are capable of destroying your ships (even in PvE) by just being overweight on your ship as it takes damage if the ship has too much cargo.  So wake up one morning, ready to set sail again, only to find your ship is at the bottom of the ocean, completely scrapped from somebody.

I don't even know what's happening in the game any more.  I have been waiting for an update to come out that would fix a lot of the issues everyone and myself have been having so that maybe I could come back and try sailing again because it's the one thing I found really fun.  But I don't think that day will come.  Don't waste your money and time on this game.

This game seemed at first to have a lot of potential. I bought it at the same time as 6 of my friends as we thought it would be fun to sail the high seas, each performing a role on our ship, and gathering loot to build bigger and better things. We built a sloop (the smallest ship) and sailed around hunting for treasure for several hours and quite enjoyed it. Then our fun was put to an end.

The game consists of 225 grid squares in a 15x15 grid, each contained in a different server. Not every grid square contains everything you need and for many reasons you will need to cross these boundaries. There are also random NPC 'damned' ships that will attack you if you get too close. After about 5 hours of sailing we crossed into another server, loading in right next to a very large, very high level NPC ship. It started firing on us almost immediately and did a huge amount of damage before we managed to turn the ship around and leave back to the other grid square/server. It followed us and sunk us in seconds, costing us hours of progress looting. We were absolutely powerless to stop it and the only way we could have feasibly prevented this happening was to send a player over the border as a 'canary' to see if it was safe, which seemed pretty ridiculous but we accepted it and made it policy to do so every time we needed to cross into another grid.

We then decided to set up somewhere on land, if we have a base of operations to set up then next time we might not lose everything. We picked a lawless zone to set up in as the player controlled islands we visited promised to kill settlers on sight. After several hours we built a small base on an island and a schooner,a medium sized ship that can hold a seemingly decent amount of weapons, to sail the seas once again. A few minutes after we set out, a very large, very high level ship with lots of cannons and weapons began to pursue us. It was much faster than ours, catching up to us quickly and once it opened up its gun ports we were done for. It obliterated us and launched a submarine to take our meagre belongings. Some of us escaped and managed to climb a ladder onto their ship. Upon close inspection their ship was made from incredibly high quality parts and their captain had about 5x more health than any of us. For a while I hid on their ship as they continued to patrol the grid square in circles, searching for more people to stomp. I consider this loss fair, however certain aspects of it highlight a major problem in the game that I will get to at the end of this review.

Despite losing the ship we still had a standing base, there wasn’t much left in it, but it was something. We were raided while offline however nothing was taken because we didn’t have anything worth taking, they left most of our walls and crafting structures. We built up the base more and started stockpiling weapons. Building a new ship was put on hold in favour of building up a large, multi layered, Rust style base. We were then attacked by a small group with horse drawn cannons and mortars. They would mostly shoot and scoot with the cannon leaving us unable to chase them. Shooting them often did not register hits despite seeing large bursts of blood coming out of them. We killed them a couple times when they approached close enough to engage in melee however they always came back. Then they set up a small bunker outside our door containing an NPC on a cannon. This cannon would snap to anyone in its firing arc and instantly kill then with a very (unrealistically) short reload time. Attacking it with multiple people from different directions lead to everyone getting obliterated in seconds. At a distance, I personally shot over 40 crossbow bolts into the gunner and saw blood splatters every time, yet he took no damage. Later I learned that NPCs take no damage while they are manning a gun. (Looking around online this seems to be intentional, although I can’t say for certain.) We had nothing we could use to kill him except for a cannon in storage saved for when we finally build another ship. I placed the cannon where the NPC didn’t shoot it and loaded it up to retaliate. I did not realise there was a 20 minute cooldown before a placed cannon is usable. In a couple minutes mortar fire came down on top of our cannon and destroyed it. We were doomed. Not because the players we were fighting were especially skilled, but because the game mechanics were rigged against us.

This event typified both of the problems we had with the game:
1. Bugs/oversights. Inability to damage things you hit, seeing blood splatters and arrows sticking out of things, particularly fish and birds, that should be taking damage but are not. One could excuse this due to the game being in early access however this problem also (from what I have heard from friends) exists in ARK too, which is from the same developers and NOT in early access. This can really make PVP difficult when the auto aim feature isn’t working. Losing our ship when crossing servers also wasn’t logical or fair either, however I understand why it happens. (Preventing the NPC ships from going near or crossing grid borders could be exploited) I think a fair fix for this is to have a short timer (1 minute or so) after changing server before a ship attacks you unless you attack it first, and if you leave within this minute and don’t attack it, the ship will not pursue you. However I do not have faith that this will be done however due to the other issues I have found in the game that have been present since ARK.

2. Game balance. The balance of the game always favours long timer players and big, well equipped groups/companies. Some might say that it is realistic that a large, heavily armed brigantine should be able to easily destroy a smaller ship that is not well armed, this is true. It is also realistic that a bullet in the head will kill someone just about all of the time. Manning a cannon does not magically make you invincible until your cannon is destroyed. Experience digging up treasure does not make you take 5x the number of gunshots in the head as someone who hasn't dug much treasure. In Atlas, guns are not the great equaliser, there is no great equaliser. In a similar game, Rust, a skilled player with a bow (a very easy weapon to make) could very easily kill a player armed with the best assault rifle and armour in the game with some well aimed and timed shots. Progression in Rust is not tied to skills and stats, but learning through blueprints to craft better (though never overpowered) gear. Spend enough time in Atlas and it seems you will be totally unstoppable to anyone who hasn’t played a similar number of hours to you.

I wanted to like this game and did have some fun with it in the beginning, but its not worth regularly losing so much progress to other players while being so powerless to stop them. The game's mechanics designed to protect the players who already have it all from those who don’t have anything. I haven’t tried this game in PVE yet so that might be more enjoyable and if I do I might change this review to be a bit more lenient. Until then I can’t recommend this game.

This is both one of the best games - and one of the worst games - I've played in 30+ years of playing video games.

The essential problem is one of direction. I'm not a PVPer (anymore) and so games with a hyper focus on PVP do not appeal to me. I'm not going to sit here and question their decision to go with PVP per se. It's a valid choice for game design and it has a dedicated fan base. And I hope the PVPers out there are having fun.

The problem with Atlas is that the developers (maybe inadvertently given their PVP focus) created the foundations for what could have been the best exploration, sailing, building, PvE MMO of all time. The game has *stupendous* potential. Playing Atlas I felt the same way I felt when I first played Sid Meier's Pirates and similar story games from the old days. It was deep. It was rich. It was immersive. It was huge.

Unfortunately, the developer felt the need to focus on its core piratical theme. And so this glorious foundation for a decade long obsession with sailing the oceans was chopped up and refactored as a PVP only experience. As an old Star Wars Galaxies fan, I felt all over again the incredible pain and disappointment of watching incredible potential be replaced by something considerably different.

I know the fact that I design games for a living (one of two jobs, anyway) doesn't make me an "expert". But it does mean I've spent thousands of hours since the 80s thinking about how to create incredible experiences for other people. It just sucks big time to see something so amazing fade and die.

So, this review isn't to bash the developers. It's not to bash PVP games or PVP players.(All gamers are awesome to me.) It's to warn those of you who like persistent, living, and open worlds filled with amazing multiplayer non-competitive gameplay... to stay away. And it pains me to say it. I loved this game.

Atlas!!  What a mixed bag this is!
Firstly, I'm a day 1 player and i have 5000 Hours in atlas, Its fair to say i've had my moneys worth and have some great memories, Atlas promoted camaraderie on a level I've rarely seen in a game. I've also made some lasting friendships. Atlas will always hold a special place in my heart.

Can i recommend the Game however?  
That's unfortunately a big fat No!
It's no secret that Grapeshot games is an offshoot of Ark's studio wildcard, and many of arks assets and systems exist in Atlas. This unfortunately means that Atlas falls under the umbrella of Fail.. I mean... Snail Games and the drama that brings.

Atlas suffers from some of the most incredibly incompetent management of development i have ever seen.
The decisions made have been staggeringly short sighted and down right stupid.

Atlas had an incredibly shaky launch and the first season was rife with performance issues and exploits, but the developers did get on top if it, For me the game peaked around season 4. It was a gem in the rough, but give it a chance it was one worth playing.
Development on atlas went quiet for about a year while the dev team were transferred over to Ark to work on Genesis 2
Eventually a new development team was brought in, they seem inexperienced but i do give them props for their effort and some really good ideas. However this is where things went downhill.
When a new team tries to pick up where the old team left of, they have different ideas, different scope, different direction.
They did not understand the dream of what we were originally sold upon.
Aditionally, the design lead at the time was a real POS of a human being.

During the infamous Barrel Bomb patch, Barrel bombs were fireable from cannons, This had been hinted at before by the new devs but the community were quick to tell them it was tried in Season 1 and was a terrible idea, they however, did it anyway.
The community was in uproar! small and medium companies were literally wiped overnight, this forced many to quit.
despite the massive community backlash, the design leads response was literally "Barrel bombs are here to stay"
Though they were eventually reballanced to a point where they were good for gameplay, it took way to long and the damage was done.

As the seasons have progressed, Atlas has drifted further away from the dream of an open world pirate game we were sold on.  To give you some examples of how the game changed for the worse..

In the early days, Discords were set up to promote trading of Blueprint materials, Cargo container for a cargo container, we even traded with our most hated enemies. It was an unintentionally interesting side effect of the resource systems in the game. That was all killed off with the introduction of the Market place and warehouse. theres now no reason to interact with other players other than to kill them.

Ships were replaced with Modular ships, this almost entirely removed any customisation or strategy in building them and reduced them to a generic design.

Ships are now viewable on the map removing any sort of stealth or the possibility of random or surprise encounters.

Lawless had a new system introduced called "Claimable lawless" which was rediculously exploitable, defences were pointless as they could be circumvented by attacking a claim tower. As such, Lawless lands are largely ghost towns as theres no point in doing anything there.

Although there has been a few good additions, they dont make up for everything the game has lost.
Its just a generic pvp slug fest now. Any sense of wonder and awe has been removed.

On a final note, the game has a development deficit of 16 Million dollars.
The writing is truly on the wall for Atlas, and its chances of Survival are slim.
I Hope they can pull it back as i really want to love Atlas again, but i doubt it.

The game is nothing like the trailer. Devs truly jebaited everyone. There are extreme design flaws in this game. 

-Every player is forced to spawn on a starter island at first. This creates a bottleneck where a fraction of players are able to even play. It is possible to buy this game and not be able to spawn.

-Half the world is tundra/polar zones where resources are scarce and you cant build basic tools. A large chunk of the zones are spawn zones where you cant build/claim land. This leaves 15% of the islands in the world ideal and habitable. They have all been claimed by large groups. 

-95% of the people who wanted to play at launch couldnt due to the servers eating ass. The people who were able to get off starter zones during this time had no issues and were able to snowball their levels and tech. 

-30 hours to travel the world means nothing when you can create a few beds and teleport between them. 

-It takes 10min to claim land and 2 hours to remove someones claim. This means larger groups are taking over multiple islands and are notified as soon as you try to unclaim their land. Without land you cant build and advance in the game. 

-You will not be able to play this game to any degree as a solo player. At least in ark you could hide, in this game you have to announce your position via claim, which shows up on the map and when pressing H. 

-All the npcs you see in the trailer dont exist in game. None of the towns are a thing and people just build boxes like Ark. 

-During the twitch streamer event there were ghost ships, floating bottles, treasure hunting. In the trailer theres mythological creature hunting, mermaids, dragons, etc. None of that exists.

-Hit registration and auto aiming features are completely trash. The game forces auto aim to a degree when meleeing. You can disable it in options and it still exists.

-Death is meaningless. You can put a bed on your raft and die over and over while sailing. You dont need to eat. Dont need to drink. Dont need to manage the completely idiotic vitamin system. Just die and respawn on your bed then harvest your corpse for hide.

-Ignore the tornados they do nothing

Overall the game is trash when it could have been amazing.

I played this game up to 100hrs. There are a lot of good parts and I actually like the idea of making the game hard and kind of unforgiving. Its kind of you are a pirate but there are no merchants to steal from.

Which brings me to the more annoying parts. It's so easy to sink a ship but really hard to rob them. It's so hard to find land to build on but so easy to steal land. Even recruited NPC cant help you save them. And it would be fun if this would happen while you are online, but no you just log in and everything is gone. Even if you had an entire island whit a castle on it! You log in and just see that all of your lands is red now.

The developers say they create a hardcore game! I like hardcore games but I just like them to be hardcore when I'm online. This game in its current state is entirely about getting f***** while your offline. And it seems like it's not implementation fault, it's the concept of the game. There is nothing about offline protection for ships, zones or players.

But it would be quite easy to change this: 

Land claiming:
Right now you paying gold for NPC but not for claiming land. The game would feel much better if you need to pay for your claimed territory.  Then not everyone would claim everywhere. Companies would not try to get as much land as they can.
As long as companies pay for their land you can't steal it. To steal the land from players, you would need to raid them first, steal their gold and afterward, if no gold left, you could steal their land. Or you need to hinder players to bring the gold from the ships to the flags to pay. Because people would need to hunt for gold frequently and the only way to get gold is by using your ships.
This would also bring the flags to the middle of the bases and make them more to an active part of the game which needs to be protected. It would also enforce to hunt players while they are online and outside of their base instead of killing them while they are sleeping in their freshly lost base.
If a company is offline the cost for the land could increase while the structures have bonus protection. Therefore the company could not stay offline forever. This would also tackle the problem with different online times from players all over the world because you would need to go for online players.
This change would empower organized companies where players have to play actively together rather than the huge unorganized companies.

Sinking Ships:
Building a ship is highly costly, sinking it is not. RIght now you can sink the most ships with 2 explosive barrels. This wouldn`t be a problem if this would happen when you are online, but it always happens when you are offline. Therefore the game needs dry docks, where it's still easy to destroy parts of the ship but destroying the entire ship is quite a huge effort. As you need to pay for the land the number of ships would be limited by the land you can spare for the dry docks. 

NPC`s food:
NPC should be paid once and/or just very little over time but should eat much more. Bigger and greener lands could feed more NPC's for your fleet. Food would become much more valuable. Bringing food to colder or desert areas would be needed which would encourage players to also play merchants. Furthermore, strong companies would not try to take just some land. They would go for the resource-rich and green ones, which will bring up fights for landmarks not just for the landmass. If the NPC's would also be affected by the vitamins, it would be even better for the in-game economy. Because the value of farming, cooking, cows, chickens etc would rise drastically.

I really like the basic game they implemented and I would love if the game gets in a good direction because it is a lot of potential in it! I would love to recommend it but I in its current state I can't. And that's because right now it's NOT a hardcore online game. Its a hardcore offline game.
If the developers take the small effort to make the needed changes I would highly recommend this game.

[h1]Where to begin with ATLAS.....[/h1]

[b]THE BAD[/b]
I could very easily shit on this game in multiple paragraphs for its insane number of bugs, poor development choices(Bad to the point of actively making the game worse with each balance change and new feature), High number of players who cheat or use exploits and not to mention the toxicity of the community who actively DOX each other, Review bomb businesses belonging to other players and create content and communities for the sole purpose of harassing other players but i'll leave it at that. This is not exclusive to Atlas, this problem is in many games like this but to me it seems especially vicious because of the small community.

[b]THE GOOD[/b]
Those of us who stuck around after the disaster of a launch and ignored all the issues listed above were rewarded for our time with a few incredible seasons where gaming communities were born, real friends were made and memories that have lasted for years were obtained.

What really sold the game for me was the level of logistics required to wage war with other company's.
Everything needed to be accounted for, Training, Supplies, Scouting, Spying, Traitors, Allies. The list goes on.
The whole game rewarded captains, pvpers and leaders who prepared for anything. Because of this some players could really make a name for themselves if they were highly skilled. 
To this day I can remember off the top of my head who the best captains and pvpers in 2019 (Season 3) were.

Back in the day, me and my company had the gaming time of our lives setting up raids, massive fleet battles, training nights or even just hanging out farming materials or building our island and ships.

[b]Conclusion[/b]
Atlas is in a very bad state right now, The new direction the game has taken has really ruined it for a lot of us and the playerbase has shrunk to the point where its essentially the same 150 players each season and I don't foresee that changing until the game eventually closes. That being said, I must give this game a thumbs up if for nothing else, it entertained me for almost 5k hours, I met hundreds of other players, Built a successful gaming community centered around Atlas, Have made Dozens of real life friends and we are all still together reading the patch notes and frowning with disappointment every time. 

We still got the memories though

There's so many things wrong with this game, but lets start with the biggest and most glaring:

- Everything you do has an utterly pointless quicktime event.

- Every island you land on is owned by a super-alliance, which means you'll spend about 99% of your time living on your boat.

- Every effort you make to try and eat food will be met with the realization that you will die because of vitamin system.

- You will spend far more time recovering from game crashes than from anything else in the game itself.

- Bugs and exploits never get fixed. And the only 'updates' the devteam provides is some jank novel garbage with the occasional "We released a new modular ship" thrown in.

- Because the game is designed to force you into playing with others, Single Player ends up being an impossible mess.

So, is this game worth it? Absolutely not. These people like to tout themselves as being "The people who made the great and fantastic Ark!" But don't let that fool you. Ark is a buggy mess plagued by greedy amateur devs ever since they released their first DLC while still in early access. This game is literally just them re-branding Ark and then selling it back to you.

In all honesty, there's so much in common with Ark and Atlas that they could have just made this a DLC to Ark rather than its own game. You're literally just buying the exact same game, but just far more unoptimized. In fact I'm almost entirely convinced that, beyond the here-and-there content release of ONE new thing, this game is just as abandoned by the devs as it is by the players.

You would think that with as much posturing as they do, they would have the funding to put their money where their mouths are.

"We made Ark! Ark is our flagship game! If you love Ark, you'll love this!"

So then why does it feel like such an under-budgeted mess? Hmm? Hmmmmm? Lets be real here. This game is just one more cash grab designed by devs who are selling you nothing except the idea that 'The people who made Ark made it.'

That's their only selling point. Not the game itself, but another game. "Buy this game! Not because it's a pirate game! But because of Ark!" That's literally it.

I wish I could suggest this game even if it was on sale, but I can't.

Save your money and steer clear of this game, along with every other game these people make!
